marks.gloss_en: בן איש חי -- are all others sons of the dead? rather, even in his death he is called living: so Benayahu's verse shows a righteous man called living in death
'son of a living man' -- are all others then sons of the dead? rather: 'son of a living man' -- that even in his death he is called living
some say: he broke blocks of hail and went down and immersed
'and the dead know nothing' -- these are the wicked
ואף רבי יונתן הדר ביה, דאמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר רבי יונתן: מנין למתים שמספרים זה עם זה -- R' Yonatan's own memra shows the dead know
whence that the dead converse with one another?

ולא ידע? והא כתיב אך בשרו עליו יכאב ונפשו עליו תאבל, ואמר רבי יצחק קשה רמה למת כמחט בבשר החי -- the dead feel pain, so they know (kind svara under protest: no ObjectionKind names the והא כתיב verse-contradiction)
and does he not know? but it is written: 'only his flesh upon him pains, and his soul upon him mourns' (Job 14:22)
אמרי: בצערא דידהו ידעי, בצערא דאחריני לא ידעי -- of their own pain they know, of others' pain they do not (= p_yodim_tzaar_atzman, p_lo_yodim_tzaar_acherim)
of their own pain they know
ולא? והתניא: מעשה בחסיד אחד... דברים שביני לבינך כבר נשמעו בין החיים -- אלמא ידעי: the dead knew what had passed among the living
דילמא איניש אחרינא שכיב ואזיל ואמר להו -- perhaps another person died and went and told them
תא שמע: דזעירי... בהדי פלניתא דאתיא למחר -- אלמא ידעי: she knew who would die tomorrow
Ze'iri's dead innkeeper: go take them [the coins] from under the door-hinge in such a place, and tell my mother to send me my comb and my tube of eye-paint with so-and-so who comes tomorrow
דלמא דומה קדים ומכריז להו -- perhaps Duma comes first and announces it to them
תא שמע: דאבוה דשמואל... דלעגל קא אתית... אלמא דידעי -- his father knew Shmuel would soon come
דילמא שאני שמואל, כיון דחשיב קדמי ומכרזי: פנו מקום -- perhaps Shmuel is different: since he is important they announce beforehand, clear a place
does our father know of this anguish?
the baraita (the pious man in the cemetery, third year): one spirit to the other: my friend, leave me -- the words between me and you have already been heard among the living
Shmuel's dead father: why do you weep? -- because you are coming [here] soon
